title: Cache and artifacts
summary: Make restore fast and keep what the build produced: the test report and the published API.

steps.title: Stage 2 briefing
body: The team has two complaints: restore takes 90 seconds every run, and when tests fail on CI nobody can see the details.
Release engineering also wants the published API as an artifact so later jobs deploy exactly what was tested.
checkout ► setup ► [cache restore] ► restore ► build ► test ─► upload test-results (always)

steps.prompt: Complete the step that uploads test results even when tests fail.
steps.explain: `dotnet test --results-directory TestResults` writes the `.trx` files there, and `always()` keeps the step from being skipped.

steps.prompt: The cache key is `${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/packages.lock.json') }}` but the repo has no `packages.lock.json`. What happens?
options: `hashFiles` returns an empty string, so the key never changes and the cache goes stale; enable lock files with `RestorePackagesWithLockFile`
Every run gets a new random key
steps.explain: Commit lock files (`<RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile>`) so the key follows real dependency changes.

steps.title: Add the cache and artifacts
prompt: 1. Before `dotnet restore`, add `actions/cache@v4` with `path: ~/.nuget/packages`, key `${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/packages.lock.json') }}`
and the restore key `${{ runner.os }}-nuget-` (as a `|` block).
2. Make the test step `dotnet test --no-build -c Release --logger trx --results-directory TestResults`.
4. Run `dotnet publish src/Api -c Release -o out --no-build` and upload `out` as artifact `api`.
Everything from stage 1 must keep working.
The program prints your workflow file. **Run checks** runs it and looks for the required lines in the output. Indentation is YAML structure, so keep it consistent (two spaces per level).
solution: - run: dotnet test --no-build -c Release --logger trx --results-directory TestResults
- run: dotnet publish src/Api -c Release -o out --no-build
hints: Each upload is its own `- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4` step with a `with:` block holding `name` and `path`.
The `if:` line goes at the same indentation as `with:`.

tests.name: - run: dotnet publish src/Api -c Release -o out --no-build
